morgan: quick note from today0: spun up Zephyrus7B (hf checkpoint) with two quant targets: int8 (per-channel) and awq-int4. noticed a nasty long-context degradation on code summarization tests. short snippets ok, but beyond ~1k tokens the model repeats and loses function names.

kevin: hmm, which conversion path? any rotary/head remapping?

morgan: used rwd-convert v0.9 default for int8 (per-channel) and awq for int4. did not change rotary params. tokenizer same as baseline (byte-level + nfkc). conversion logs look normal.

chandra: repetition after 1k often points to KV-cache indexing or rotary phase mismatch. do logits diverge gradually or catastrophically?

morgan: logits start similar then diverge after about 1.1k tokens. ran a difflog of attention scores and saw the attention magnitude drop on specific heads in the later layers when using int8. head 9 and head 14 show near-zero attention energy post-quant.

sophia: can you paste the small probe + commands? also include a head-level attention dump.

morgan: paste below:
```
# convert commands
rwd-convert --src zephyrus7b/fp16.ckpt --dst zephyrus7b-int8.perch.quant \
  --method per_channel_int8 --block-size 128 --calib-samples 2048

rwd-convert --src zephyrus7b/fp16.ckpt --dst zephyrus7b-awq-int4.quant \
  --method awq --block-size 128 --calib-samples 1024 --headwise-quant true

# eval reproducer
rwd-infer --model zephyrus7b-int8.perch.quant --task code-sum \
  --max-tokens 2048 --prompt-file tests/longcode/large-func.py --dump-attn heads=all --batch 1
```

# truncated head energy diff (last layer)
float16: [0.13, 0.11, 0.12, 0.09, 0.10, 0.11, 0.12, 0.13, 0.14, 0.12, 0.11, 0.10, 0.09, 0.12, 0.13, 0.11]
int8:    [0.12, 0.10, 0.11, 0.09, 0.10, 0.11, 0.00, 0.01, 0.02, 0.00, 0.01, 0.00, 0.00, 0.01, 0.02, 0.00]

kevin: wow head collapse on int8 for several heads. that suggests per-channel scale underflow for those projection rows or a mismatch in head ordering during re-shard. any evidence of head permute applied in conversion?

morgan: converter debug shows no headperm step. but the upstream checkpoint has an odd "qkv_layout": "nhp" vs our canonical "hnp" for that family. we do have a small shim that canonicalizes qkv layout during load, but maybe the int8 path bottoms out when scales are computed against the wrong axis.

chandra: important: quantization scale axes must match the projection layout. if we compute scales across incorrect dims you can zero out an entire head. try re-run conversion with explicit qkv-layout override to 'hnp' and recompute scales. also run a short per-head scale histogram check.

morgan: kicking two runs now: (A) int8 with qkv-layout forced hnp, (B) int8 with per-channel scale clamp min=1e-4. also running an awq-int4 headwise check where we skip quantizing heads 7,8,9 (suspect heads) to see if behaviour recovers.

ci-bot: job 51011 queued (node=gpu-b3), est 9m

eval-bot: started run 51011 subset=code-longctx (100 examples)

[8m later]

morgan: quick results (100 ex):
- int8 (orig) => repeat@1k 67/100, code-ROUGE 42.1, latency p50 120ms
- int8 (qkv-layout=hnp) => repeat@1k 12/100, ROUGE 58.3, latency p50 125ms
- int8 (scale-clamp=1e-4) => repeat@1k 15/100, ROUGE 57.9
- awq-int4 (skip heads 7-9 quant) => repeat@1k 10/100, ROUGE 59.2, p50 68ms
- fp16 baseline => repeat@1k 7/100, ROUGE 61.0, p50 210ms

kevin: great signal. the qkv layout mismatch looks like the primary root cause for int8 head collapse. clamp helps slightly but layout fix recovers most quality. interesting that awq-int4 skipping a few heads recovers as well  implies sensitivity in those projection rows to quantization.

sophia: can you add a short unit test to converter: if checkpoint.metadata.qkv_layout != expected, emit warning and require explicit override in non-interactive runs, and add a histogram check after scale computation to fail if >5% heads have scale < threshold.

morgan: will do. also adding a short note to the Zephyrus model card: "recommended conversion flags: --qkv-layout hnp --per-channel-scale-clamp 1e-4; consider head-exclusion for awq-int4 if headwise energy collapses".

chandra: follow-up: we should add a lightweight long-context code-smoke to the onboarding suite (1-2 examples) to catch repeat-onset regressions early. make it required for int8/awq.

ci-bot: created PR #8123 (converter: qkv-layout warning + scale-histogram gate)

morgan: PR #8123 opened, tests added, will link calibration plots. tagging @kevin @sophia for review.

kevin: thumbs up from me. also let's add a small head-importance map to the artifact (per-head pre-quant norms) so downstream can decide head exclusion cheaply.

sophia: agreed. also logging this for the onboarding checklist: qkv-layout parity, per-head scale histogram, long-context smoke.

morgan: thanks all, saving the int8-awq notes to the model card and uploading the calibration artifacts to the model repo.
